proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched all-design/all-estimator finite-population endpoint MSE frontier, terminating absolute-epsilon certificates, the full B=1 exact equality slice, and a strict unequal-count witness at (C,m,B,beta)=(2,100,3,1). tldr: A singleton holdout observes the untreated outcome with every peer treated exactly. Pooling controls samples more units while displacing their peer exposure from that endpoint. For bounded unit-specific Hölder tables, the proved unrestricted minimax risk has order \(\max\{B^{-1},\min\{C^{-1},(Cm)^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}\}\}\), uniformly over the finite parameter range. A computable integer-count allocation attains this order, and the converse covers every outcome-blind joint design and every full-record estimator. Exact finite risk can nevertheless improve beyond the fully optimized equal-count menu: at \((C,m,B,\beta)=(2,100,3,1)\), an explicit mixture of counts \((2,1)\) and \((1,2)\) has risk at most \(17689/108900\), while the equal-count optimum is at least \(3333/20000\). Throughout \(B=1\), both optima equal \(1/4\). For rational inputs a separate terminating algorithm supplies absolute-risk primal and finite-prior dual certificates and semidecides strict improvement; the general exact equality-versus-improvement classification remains open. The application is prospective saturation planning for bounded real-valued responses.
gap: Existing saturation planning evaluates standard errors or known-exposure regression objectives. Unrestricted network minimax theory does not directly preserve informative off-target Hölder outcomes under a hard control cap.
fill: A computable assignment and finite risk bound are paired with an all-design converse retaining the realized finite target and the full assignment record; a terminating finite-risk algorithm with explicit primal and dual certificates is posed separately.
